summary: Phase 4 (Real Believe royalty CSV + sensitive-field redaction + reset-demo-data) — 31/31 pytest passed and all frontend assertions verified against live preview URL. Backend covers: parse_amount for 13 number formats including the headline bug 0,000407547753 -> 0.000407547753, parse_csv_bytes semicolon auto-detect with all 21 Believe Indonesian headers, detect_columns mapping every canonical key (including kuantias typo, pendapatan bersih/kotor, harga unit, biaya mekanis, tingkat pembagian klien, jenis penjualan/langganan), parse_period_from_value across 6 formats, strip_sensitive removes all 4 admin-only keys, real-CSV upload of first 99 Believe rows (semicolon, EU decimals) — total_revenue_eur sums Pendapatan Bersih NOT Kotor (verified by recomputing both locally), label_name fallback match observed alongside isrc/upc matches, GET /api/royalty/lines as LABEL strips gross_revenue_eur/unit_price_eur/mechanical_cost_eur/client_share_rate while admin GET /admin/imports/{id} still includes them, POST /royalty/admin/reset-demo-data returns 400 on wrong confirm, 422 on missing confirm, 403 for admin_finance and 401/403 unauthenticated. Frontend smoke: /admin/royalty shows new 'Reset Data Demo' button next to 'Upload CSV', clicking it opens red-bordered modal listing what will be deleted, submit button is DISABLED with empty input and with lowercase 'reset', ENABLED only when user types exactly 'RESET'. Label royalty page /label/royalty (Khizanah Kreasi Gontor, 3334 lines, Rp 176.121 total) shows TotalRoyalti/TotalStreams/TotalLines, Per Platform, Top Country, Top Tracks, lines table with only Periode/Track/Artist/Platform/Country/Streams/Status/Royalti IDR columns. Live network fetch of /api/royalty/lines from the label browser session returned 0 leaked sensitive keys — sample_keys list confirms gross_revenue_eur/unit_price_eur/mechanical_cost_eur/client_share_rate are absent. Cleaned up 2 throw-away 2099-01 test imports + 198 lines via direct Mongo delete (no DELETE endpoint exists for imports).

minor.issue: No delete endpoint exists. Test imports cannot be cleaned via API; required direct Mongo cleanup. Consider adding admin-only delete for pending_review imports so QA / admins can roll back mis-uploads without nuking everything via reset-demo-data.

Detail message in code is 'Konfirmasi tidak cocok. Ketik \'RESET\' untuk melanjutkan.' (with single quotes around RESET); request payload says 'Ketik RESET untuk melanjutkan' (no quotes). Cosmetic, but make frontend/backend strings consistent if any UI parser depends on exact string.

(Optional) Reconcile error string between server.py ("Ketik 'RESET' untuk melanjutkan") and PRD wording ("Ketik RESET untuk melanjutkan"). Either is fine.

critical_code_review_comments: royalty_utils.parse_csv_bytes: row dict is built using normalized header as key, so duplicate column headers (rare in Believe but possible in user uploads) silently overwrite earlier values. Consider warning when len(set(normalized_headers)) != len(normalized_headers).

server.py upload-csv: total_revenue_eur is computed by summing every row's Pendapatan Bersih INCLUDING unmatched lines. Correct given today's UX (admin sees gross EUR before publishing), but if business later wants 'matched-only EUR' for forecasting, expose both numbers in the import doc.

server.py reset-demo-data: nukes ALL royalty_imports + royalty_lines + balance_transactions of type royalty_*, but does NOT touch withdraw_requests or releases/tracks/labels. Comment in code is accurate. Note: there is no dry-run/preview mode — single confirm string is the only safety net. For production, consider adding a 5-second hold + secondary password re-entry.

server.py upload-csv: file is written to disk under {import_id}.csv before insert. If the insert_many fails midway, the .csv file is orphaned. Reset-demo-data does purge /uploads/csv/*.csv so this is self-healing for demo data, but for production a transactional cleanup (or write-after-success) is safer.

Frontend RoyaltyImport.jsx: reset-confirm input uses local state and is reset to '' only on modal close path that hits onClick={() => setResetOpen(false)}. If user closes via ESC there's no listener — verified that ESC does close the modal but resetConfirm is not cleared, so reopening pre-fills the previous text. Minor UX nit (still works correctly because submit is gated on exact match).
